citations.venue: Forecasting Research Institute, 'Roots of Disagreement on AI Risk' (11 March 2024)
citations.figure: n=22 (concerned group: 11 participants, all domain experts; skeptic group: 11, comprising 9 superforecasters and 2 domain experts), studied over 8 weeks in April-May 2023, with median engagement of 80 hours (skeptics) and 31 hours (concerned). Median forecast of existential catastrophe by 2100 fell from 25% to 20% in the concerned group and moved from 0.10% to 0.12% in the skeptic group — a gap of more than two orders of magnitude that structured persuasion did not close. Existential catastrophe was defined as humanity going extinct or experiencing 'unrecoverable collapse' (sustained global GDP below $1 trillion annually, or human population below 1 million, for a million years, beginning before 2100). The parent XPT report records the same result at tournament scale: 'Few minds were changed during the XPT, even among the most active participants, and despite monetary incentives for persuading others.'

audit.claim: Citation 3 — 'Katja Grace, John Salvatier, Allan Dafoe, Baobao Zhang, Owain Evans (AI Impacts wiki compilation of surveys of experts on levels of AI risk) (2017), AI Impacts Wiki' — 2016 survey n=352/1,634 (21.5%), median 5%, 40% at ≥10%; Zhang et al. 2019 524/2,652 (19.7%), median 2%; Grace et al. 2022 N=738, median 5%, mean 14%, 48% at ≥10%.
audit.note: THE NUMBERS ARE ALL CORRECT — I retrieved the wiki page and it states 352 of 1,634 (21.5%), median 5%, 40% at ≥10% for 2016; 524 of 2,652 (19.7%), median 2% for Zhang 2019; 738 of ~4,271 (17.3%), median 5%, 48% at ≥10% for 2022. The fault is citation hygiene, and it is exactly the pattern this audit is meant to catch: the cited artefact is an anonymous, undated AI Impacts wiki page, and the packet puts five named individuals in the author slot with a year (2017) that belongs to neither the wiki page nor the JAIR publication. Grace, Salvatier, Dafoe, Zhang and Evans did not write that wiki page. Crossref confirms the underlying paper is real and correctly described in the packet's own source field: JAIR 62:729–754 (2018), doi 10.1613/jair.1.11222, those five authors — so cite that (or arXiv:1705.08807) for the 2016 figures and cite the wiki page as an unattributed compilation. One further nit: the packet's question wording renders the paper's bracketed '[high-level machine intelligence]' as 'this'.
audit.corrected: AI Impacts, 'Surveys of experts on levels of AI risk', AI Impacts Wiki (no named authors, undated wiki page), https://wiki.aiimpacts.org/uncategorized/ai_risk_surveys — for the underlying 2016 survey: Katja Grace, John Salvatier, Allan Dafoe, Baobao Zhang & Owain Evans, 'Viewpoint: When Will AI Exceed Human Performance? Evidence from AI Experts', Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research 62:729–754 (2018), doi 10.1613/jair.1.11222.

hazards.uncertainty:
The disagreement IS the result, and it is not a disagreement about severity — it is a disagreement about rate. Divide each XPT group's AI-extinction median by its AI-catastrophe median and the implied conditional probability of extinction given catastrophe is 0.18 (superforecasters) and 0.25 (domain experts): nearly the same. But the unconditional rates differ by a factor of 8 (catastrophe) and 8 (extinction), and Ord's own credence sits another 3.3x above the domain experts. A simulator that averages these camps is reporting a number no participant holds.

Where this packet is weakest, in the order a serious critic would attack it:
(1) The annualisation is a fiction. Every source gives a by-2100 cumulative probability; -ln(1-p)/78 assumes a constant hazard, and both camps explicitly do not believe that. The near-term rate is probably overstated several-fold and the 2070-2100 rate understated.
(2) Elicitation format moves these numbers by six orders of magnitude. The XPT's own parallel public survey (912 college graduates) gave a 2% median for AI-caused extinction by 2100 when asked for a percentage, and a median of 1 in 30 MILLION for the same event when asked to fill in X in '1-in-X', after being shown reference classes such as a 1-in-300,000 lifetime chance of being killed by lightning. Total extinction went from 5% to 1 in 15 million; catastrophe from 11.56% to 1 in 2,500. This was the public, not the forecasters, but it is the single most damning methodological fact in this literature and nobody has shown the expert samples are immune.
(3) Question wording moves the expert numbers by 2x. Grace et al. asked three near-identical extinction questions of disjoint subsamples and got medians of 5%, 10% and 5%; the 'human inability to control' framing reliably doubles the 'future AI advances' framing. Their HLMI timelines moved by a factor of two on fixed-year versus fixed-probability framing.
(4) Selection. Grace et al.'s response rate is 15% (2,778 of 18,459 functioning addresses); the authors defend it as normal for a >20,000-person invitation list and report finding no evidence of strong participation bias, but a survey about AI risk sent to AI researchers has an obvious differential-interest problem that no analysis inside the survey can fully rule out. The XPT expert sample is worse in a different way: 42% of experts (versus 9% of superforecasters) reported having attended an Effective Altruism meetup, and 44% of experts spent more than 200 hours on existential-risk work in the prior year versus 11% of superforecasters. The 'experts' are, in substantial part, a community with a prior commitment to the proposition being estimated. Symmetrically, superforecaster status was earned on short-horizon geopolitical questions with feedback, and there is no evidence it transfers to 78-year questions that can never be scored in a forecaster's lifetime; the XPT report states this counter-argument itself.
(5) Aggregation choice changes the answer by 4x within a single group. Table 4 of the XPT: AI domain experts' AI-extinction risk is 3% by median but 13.61% by arithmetic mean and 1.33% by geometric mean of odds. Reporting 'the expert estimate' as a single number conceals this.
(6) n=29 AI experts. That is the actual sample behind the 3% figure everyone quotes.
(7) Ord's 1 in 10 is one person's credence, published as a round number, and the author declined to update it numerically in 2024. It should never be treated as an elicitation result.
(8) The severity-tier split between 'major catastrophe' and 'collapse' (0.52 / 0.22 / 0.05 / 0.21) is an AUTHOR-ESTIMATE. No published source decomposes AI catastrophe severity above the >=10%-deaths threshold; only the extinction/catastrophe ratio is data-derived, and even that is a ratio of two independent medians rather than a coherent individual conditional.
(9) The XPT catastrophe question does not separate loss of control from deliberate misuse. This hazard and 'ai-enabled-misuse' therefore double-count; a simulator should not sum them.
(10) The CAIS statement carries no number and cannot be converted into one. Its evidential content is that a large set of people with direct technical knowledge and, in several cases, strong commercial incentives to say the opposite were willing to put their names to the extinction framing. A critic will note the reverse reading with equal force — that a statement costing nothing to sign, from parties who benefit from their products being described as world-historically powerful, is weak evidence about the world and strong evidence about an industry's positioning. Both readings are available and neither is quantitative. This packet does not assert a signatory count, because no primary page states one.

hazards.name: AI-enabled misuse (bioweapon design assistance, autonomous weapons, mass persuasion, authoritarian entrenchment)
hazards.oneLine: Humans deliberately use AI systems to lower the capability barrier to mass-casualty attack, to remove humans from lethal decision loops, or to make populations permanently uncontestable.
hazards.mechanism: Four distinct near-term mechanisms with different kill chains, sharing only the tool. (a) Bioweapon design assistance: the barrier to a mass-casualty biological attack has never been information, it has been tacit laboratory skill, agent acquisition and aerosolisation; the concern is that a sufficiently capable model collapses the protocol-troubleshooting portion of that barrier, moving a scenario from state-scale to small-group-scale. Death then arrives through an engineered pathogen and, above a few percent mortality, through the collapse of health systems and food distribution rather than through the pathogen alone. (b) Autonomous weapons: the mechanism is not a robot uprising but the removal of the human deliberation that currently caps engagement rate and escalation speed — automated systems on both sides of a confrontation can complete an escalation cycle faster than any political process can interrupt it, with nuclear-armed states as the terminal case. (c) Mass persuasion: personalised, conversational, cheap argument at population scale degrades the shared factual substrate a society needs to notice and respond to any of the other hazards in this packet; it kills nobody directly and raises every other hazard's severity by degrading the response. (d) Authoritarian entrenchment: comprehensive monitoring plus predictive policing removes the coordination window that historically ends bad regimes, converting a recoverable political failure into a permanent one — the only pathway here that is terminal without being lethal.

rate.eventDefinition: A mass-casualty event (>=1,000 deaths) in which AI assistance was materially causal to the perpetrator's capability — that is, the attack would not have been feasible for that actor without it. THIS IS AN AUTHOR ESTIMATE AND IS NOT DRAWN FROM ANY PUBLISHED FIGURE. No such event has occurred. The observed count is 0 over roughly four years of widely available frontier LLMs, which places essentially no upper constraint (a zero-count over 4 years bounds the rate only below ~0.75/yr at 95%). The estimate is anchored downward by the RAND red-team null result and upward by the fact that frontier developers have already begun activating heightened safeguards on the strength of internal evaluations they will not fully publish. Treat the range as spanning two and a half orders of magnitude because that is genuinely the state of knowledge.
rate.trend: Rising, and this is the one place in the packet where the trend is better evidenced than the level. RAND (January 2024) found no measurable uplift from the then-current LLM generation. Sixteen months later (22 May 2025) Anthropic activated its ASL-3 CBRN deployment and security standard for Claude Opus 4, stating it had 'not yet determined whether Claude Opus 4 has definitively passed the Capabilities Threshold that requires ASL-3 protections' and was acting 'as a precautionary and provisional action' in light of continued improvements in CBRN-related knowledge and capabilities. The direction of travel between those two data points is unambiguous; the magnitude is not measured by either.

rateMods.why: capability proxy. Note the honest anchor underneath: RAND's red-team study found NO statistically significant biological uplift from current models, so the measured value of the uplift ratio is 1.0 — this hazard's rate is an extrapolation, not a measurement — reference point solved at build time (277.6) so that the mean multiplier over 100 years is exactly 1: the cited rate was annualised from a by-2100 figure, so its century total must be preserved while the shape is allowed to rise

tiers.label: Contained incident
tiers.desc: 1,000 to ~100,000 deaths: a single successful attack, a localised outbreak, or an autonomous-weapons engagement gone wrong. Contained by conventional public-health or military response. The dominant real-world consequence is regulatory — this is the tier that produces the international agreement, the export controls, and the mandatory pre-deployment evaluation regime.
tiers.split: contained incident

tiers.label: Regional mass-casualty event or limited pandemic
tiers.desc: 0.5-5% of world population. An engineered agent escapes containment regionally, or an automated escalation produces a conventional war with a mass-casualty exchange. Health systems in affected regions fail; global supply chains are disrupted but not broken.
tiers.split: regional mass-casualty event or limited pandemic

tiers.label: Global catastrophe
tiers.desc: >=10% of world population within five years — the XPT catastrophe threshold. An engineered pathogen with both high transmissibility and high case-fatality, or a nuclear exchange reached through an automated escalation cycle. Most of the deaths above the direct toll come from the failure of food and medical distribution in the following two growing seasons.
tiers.split: global catastrophe, dominated by the biological sub-mechanism

tiers.label: Terminal release
tiers.desc: An engineered agent optimised simultaneously for transmissibility, latency and lethality — the combination natural selection does not produce because it is not adaptive for the pathogen. Population falls below the threshold for maintaining any industrial society and does not recover.
tiers.split: terminal release

cascades.why: the dominant sub-mechanism — this hazard is mostly a route INTO that one
same capability frontier, same deployment surface
automated escalation compresses the decision cycle below the time a human needs

citations.claim: Frontier LLMs as of the 2023-24 generation gave no measurable uplift in biological attack planning
citations.authors: Christopher A. Mouton, Caleb Lucas, Ella Guest
citations.venue: RAND Corporation, report RR-A2977-2, doi 10.7249/RRA2977-2, published 25 January 2024, 24 pp. (final results; preceded by RR-A2977-1, 16 October 2023)
citations.figure: 'The findings indicate that using the existing generation of LLMs did not measurably change the operational risk of such an attack.' Key takeaways, verbatim: 'This research involving multiple LLMs indicates that biological weapon attack planning currently lies beyond the capability frontier of LLMs as assistive tools. The authors found no statistically significant difference in the viability of plans generated with or without LLM assistance.' And, as a stated limitation: 'This research did not measure the distance between the existing LLM capability frontier and the knowledge needed for biological weapon attack planning.' Design: an expert exercise in which teams role-playing malign non-state actors were assigned realistic scenarios and tasked with planning a biological attack; some teams had an LLM plus the internet, others the internet only. The authors note they would want to 'increase the sensitivity of these tests by expanding the number of LLMs tested, involving more researchers, and removing unhelpful sources of variability.'

citations.claim: A frontier developer activated heightened CBRN safeguards in 2025 without having confirmed the capability threshold was crossed — evidence of trend direction, and of the limits of public evidence
citations.authors: Anthropic
citations.venue: Anthropic, 'Activating AI Safety Level 3 Protections', 22 May 2025
citations.figure: 'We have not yet determined whether Claude Opus 4 has definitively passed the Capabilities Threshold that requires ASL-3 protections.' The model was deployed under the ASL-3 Deployment and Security Standard 'as a precautionary and provisional action'; the stated reason is continued improvements in CBRN-related knowledge and capabilities making the risk impossible to rule out, with initial focus on biological weapons. Claude Sonnet 4 was kept at the ASL-2 standard. This is a first-party statement by an interested developer, published without the underlying evaluation data, and should be treated as an indicator of direction rather than as a measurement of uplift.

citations.claim: Personalised LLM persuasion measurably exceeds human persuasion in direct conversation
citations.authors: Francesco Salvi, Manoel Horta Ribeiro, Riccardo Gallotti, Robert West
citations.venue: arXiv:2403.14380, 'On the Conversational Persuasiveness of Large Language Models: A Randomized Controlled Trial'; published as 'On the conversational persuasiveness of GPT-4', Nature Human Behaviour 9(8):1645-1653 (2025), doi 10.1038/s41562-025-02194-6
citations.figure: 'We found that participants who debated GPT-4 with access to their personal information had 81.7% (p < 0.01; N=820 unique participants) higher odds of increased agreement with their opponents compared to participants who debated humans. Without personalization, GPT-4 still outperforms humans, but the effect is lower and statistically non-significant (p=0.31).' Pre-registered two-by-two factorial design: human-vs-human or human-vs-LLM opponent, crossed with personalisation on or off (basic sociodemographic information about the opponent). Figures quoted are from the arXiv preprint retrieved directly; the peer-reviewed Nature Human Behaviour version reports the same experiment with an expanded design and a slightly different N.

citations.claim: The only documented battlefield use of a loitering munition described by the UN as a lethal autonomous weapons system — and what the primary document does and does not say
citations.authors: UN Panel of Experts on Libya, Letter dated 8 March 2021 to the President of the Security Council, UN doc S/2021/229 (reproduced in the ICRC 'How does law protect in war?' online casebook)
citations.venue: United Nations Security Council / ICRC casebook
citations.figure: Para. 63: 'The lethal autonomous weapons systems were programmed to attack targets without requiring data connectivity between the operator and the munition: in effect, a true "fire, forget and find" capability.' Para. 64 records that retreating Haftar Affiliated Forces 'were subject to continual harassment from the unmanned combat aerial vehicles and lethal autonomous weapons systems' and 'suffered significant casualties.' The system named is the STM Kargu-2. CRITICAL READING: the report attributes a capability, not an executed autonomous engagement. It does not state that the system selected or engaged a human target without operator involvement, and does not attribute any specific death to autonomous operation. The frequently repeated 'first autonomous kill in history' framing is not supported by the primary text.

citations.claim: How published AI researchers rank the near-term misuse mechanisms against each other
citations.authors: Katja Grace, Harlan Stewart, Julia Fabienne Sandkühler, Stephen Thomas, Ben Weinstein-Raun, Jan Brauner, Richard C. Korzekwa
citations.venue: arXiv:2401.02843; Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research vol. 84 (2025), doi 10.1613/jair.1.19087
citations.figure: Respondents (n=1,345) were asked about eleven potentially concerning AI scenarios. 'Each scenario was considered worthy of either substantial or extreme concern by more than 30% of respondents.' Ranked by the share rating substantial or extreme concern: spread of false information e.g. deepfakes 86%; manipulation of large-scale public opinion trends 79%; AI letting dangerous groups make powerful tools (e.g. engineered viruses) 73%; authoritarian rulers using AI to control their populations 73%; AI systems worsening economic inequality (also among the top five). Separately, on the meta-question 'To what extent do you think people's concerns about future risks from AI are due to misunderstandings of AI research?' (n=671): 10.7% 'Almost entirely', 44% 'To a large extent', 29.1% 'Somewhat', 14.6% 'Not much', 1.6% 'Hardly at all' — i.e. a majority of AI researchers think public concern is substantially rooted in misunderstanding, while a majority of the same population assigns >=5% to extinction-level outcomes. Both facts are in the same survey.

audit.claim: Citation 4 — UN Panel of Experts on Libya, S/2021/229, 8 March 2021 — para. 63 'fire, forget and find'; and 'Para. 64 records that retreating Haftar Affiliated Forces were subject to continual harassment… and suffered significant casualties.'
audit.note: I retrieved the ICRC casebook page in full. The paragraph-63 quote is EXACT and correctly located: 'The lethal autonomous weapons systems were programmed to attack targets without requiring data connectivity between the operator and the munition: in effect, a true "fire, forget and find" capability.' The document number, date, the STM Kargu-2 identification, and the packet's central CRITICAL READING (the report attributes a capability, not an executed autonomous engagement, and supports no 'first autonomous kill' claim) are all correct and well made. But the second half of the paragraph-64 claim misreads the primary text. The subject of 'These suffered significant casualties' is the Pantsir S-1 surface-to-air missile systems named in the immediately preceding clause — the trailing qualifier 'even when used in a passive electro-optical role to avoid GNA-AF jamming' can only describe equipment, not retreating soldiers. The packet's wording matches The Verge's paraphrase, which is reproduced as Document B on the very same casebook page ('the HAF "suffered significant casualties" as a result'), so the error looks like it entered via the secondary source rather than from the UN text. The effect is to make a hazard packet on AI-enabled mass casualties appear to have a primary-source human-casualty attribution that the primary source does not make — which is precisely the over-reading the citation's own caveat warns against. Fix: quote para. 64 only for 'continual harassment', and drop the casualty clause or attribute it to the air-defence systems. https://casebook.icrc.org/case-study/libya-use-lethal-autonomous-weapon-systems
audit.corrected: Para. 64 actually reads: 'Once in retreat, they were subject to continual harassment from the unmanned combat aerial vehicles and lethal autonomous weapons systems, which were proving to be a highly effective combination in defeating the […] Pantsir S-1 surface-to-air missile systems. These suffered significant casualties, even when used in a passive electro-optical role to avoid GNA-AF jamming.' — 'These suffered significant casualties' refers to the Pantsir S-1 air-defence systems, not to HAF personnel.

hazards.uncertainty:
The honest headline: THE ANNUAL PROBABILITY IN THIS HAZARD IS AN AUTHOR ESTIMATE, NOT A PUBLISHED FIGURE. No source consulted publishes a rate for AI-materially-causal mass-casualty attacks, and the observed count is zero, so the number is a prior with a two-and-a-half-order-of-magnitude range, not a measurement. It should be labelled as such wherever a simulator surfaces it, and it should not be presented alongside the XPT and Grace figures as if it had the same standing.

What IS well evidenced here is the mechanism inventory and the direction of travel; what is not evidenced is any rate.

Specific attack surfaces a critic will use:
(1) The RAND null is underpowered by its own authors' admission, and it measures the wrong thing for forecasting: it tested the 2023-24 model generation, and explicitly did not measure the gap between that frontier and the capability that would matter. Citing it as reassurance is a misreading; citing it as a base rate is the correct use.
(2) The counterweight to RAND is first-party and unaudited. Anthropic's ASL-3 activation is a company's statement about its own product, published without the evaluation data, by an organisation with a commercial interest in its models being understood as powerful. It is genuine evidence of what an internal evaluation showed, and it is also marketing-adjacent. Both are true.
(3) The autonomous-weapons literature is contaminated by a widely repeated claim the primary document does not make. S/2021/229 describes a capability, not a confirmed autonomous engagement, and several secondary sources have converted this into 'the first autonomous kill'. Any model calibrated on that claim is calibrated on an artefact of press coverage.
(4) The persuasion result is a real, pre-registered RCT with a real effect, on a short online debate with sociodemographic personalisation, over topics of varying opinion strength. Generalising an 81.7% odds increase in that setting to population-scale epistemic degradation is a leap the paper does not make and this packet does not have evidence for. The link from persuasion effect size to any mortality figure is entirely an author assumption.
(5) The authoritarian-entrenchment pathway has the weakest quantitative footing of the four and the strongest claim to being terminal. The knob offered is a measure of researcher concern, not of adoption, because no adoption figure was located; a simulator that treats 73% as a deployment share is making an error this packet is explicitly trying to prevent.
(6) The severity tier probabilities (0.80 / 0.16 / 0.035 / 0.005) are author estimates with no source. They encode the judgement that most successful misuse events are contained and that the jump to a >=10%-mortality event requires an agent with a transmissibility-lethality combination that natural selection does not favour — which is an argument, not a measurement.
(7) Overlap with 'unaligned-ai' is real and unresolved. The XPT's 2.13%/12% AI-catastrophe figures cover misuse and loss of control together. If a simulator uses that rate for the unaligned-ai hazard and then adds this hazard's rate on top, it is double-counting. The correct treatment is either to use this hazard as a decomposition of the unaligned-ai rate, or to run them as alternative framings of the same event.

hazards.name: Biosphere degradation: pollinator, soil, aquifer and fishery loss
hazards.oneLine: The chronic erosion of the biological and physical capital that agriculture stands on, which so far lowers the system's buffer against shocks rather than lowering output.
hazards.mechanism: Nothing in biosphere degradation kills people directly, and any model in which it does is wrong on the observed record. It works by thinning the stock of free inputs agriculture draws on: animal pollination underwrites 35% of global production volume, though only 13 of 107 crops assessed by Klein et al. lose 90% or more without pollinators and none of those are the wind- or self-pollinated cereals that supply most calories; conventional tillage removes topsoil at roughly 1 mm/yr against soil production one to two orders of magnitude slower; irrigation is mining stored groundwater that does not recharge on human timescales (286.4 million acre-feet gone from the High Plains aquifer, about 9% of recoverable storage, with an area-weighted decline of 16.5 ft); and marine capture has fallen from 90% of assessed stocks fished within biologically sustainable levels in 1974 to 62.4% by 2023. Every one of these losses is compensable in the short run by more synthetic nitrogen, more pumping energy, more land and more fishing effort, which is exactly why world agricultural output rose nearly fourfold between 1961 and 2020 on only 7.6% more land while output per capita rose 53%. The compensations are bought with inputs, and the inputs are concentrated: 48% of the world population is fed on Haber-Bosch nitrogen, and 68% of phosphate rock reserves sit in a single country. So the causal chain to mass death runs entirely through a later shock: degradation converts a system with slack into a system already running at the edge of its substitutes, so that when a harvest failure arrives the floor it falls onto is lower and the compensating levers are already pulled. Deaths, when they come, are famine deaths and infectious-disease deaths in malnourished import-dependent populations, not deaths from the loss of a bee.

rate.eventDefinition: Onset in a given year of a further discrete degradation step, defined as a 5-percentage-point reduction in attainable global crop calorie supply relative to a no-degradation counterfactual, sustained for at least 10 years. This is NOT the probability of any deaths; it is the probability of the buffer-reducing event that other hazards in this packet draw on.
rate.trend: Rising in the aggregate but decelerating in several components. Fish stock sustainability fell ~0.57 pp/yr on average from 1974 to 2023 and is still falling (64.5% to 62.4% between the 2024 and 2026 SOFIA assessments). HANPP rose from 15.7% to 23.5% of potential natural NPP between 1950 and 2020 (~0.11 pp/yr). Against this, stratospheric ozone is recovering (284.6 DU vs a 290 DU preindustrial base) and no-till adoption cuts erosion by roughly an order of magnitude where adopted, so the trend is a policy variable, not a physical constant.

rateMods.why: degradation steps arrive faster in a warmer world — reference point solved at build time (2.710) so that the mean multiplier over 100 years is exactly 1: the cited rate was annualised from a by-2100 figure, so its century total must be preserved while the shape is allowed to rise

tiers.label: Absorbed by inputs
tiers.desc: The degradation step is fully offset by fertiliser, irrigation energy, managed pollination, and yield genetics, exactly as every step of the last sixty years has been. Global cereal yields and per-capita output keep rising. Excess mortality is confined to micronutrient-deficiency disease in populations losing access to pollinator-dependent fruits, nuts and vegetables and to small-scale fish protein — a nutrition-quality effect, not a calorie effect.
tiers.split: absorbed by inputs — 20% prompt, the rest through food

tiers.label: Regionally binding
tiers.desc: Specific regions cross their local thresholds rather than the global aggregate moving. High Plains irrigated area converts to dryland as saturated thickness falls below pumping viability; North China Plain deep-aquifer districts retire cropland; thin-soil tropical uplands lose their A horizon; small-scale fisheries collapse. Those regions flip from net exporters to net importers, tightening world trade in normal years and leaving less slack for a bad one.
tiers.split: regionally binding

tiers.label: Yield ceiling falls
tiers.desc: Global attainable yield growth turns negative for a decade despite maximal input use — the input treadmill stops paying. Total factor productivity growth, which already fell from 1.99%/yr (2001-10) to 1.12%/yr (2011-20), goes to zero or below. Chronic import dependence in low-income countries becomes structural and the reserve buffer for a food-system shock is spent in normal years rather than held for a bad one.
tiers.split: the yield ceiling falls. The honest shape of this hazard: it does not kill directly, it removes the buffer that everything else is absorbed by

cascades.why: the primary and arguably only important effect

citations.claim: Fraction of leading global food crops and of global production volume dependent on animal pollination
citations.authors: Alexandra-Maria Klein, Bernard E. Vaissiere, James H. Cane, Ingolf Steffan-Dewenter, Saul A. Cunningham, Claire Kremen, Teja Tscharntke
citations.venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B 274(1608): 303-313, DOI 10.1098/rspb.2006.3721
citations.figure: Fruit, vegetable or seed production from 87 of the leading global food crops is dependent upon animal pollination, while 28 crops do not rely upon animal pollination. Global production volumes give a contrasting perspective: 60% of global production comes from crops that do not depend on animal pollination, 35% from crops that depend on pollinators, and 5% are unevaluated. Of 107 globally important crops classified by degree of dependence: 13 essential (>=90% production loss without pollinators), 30 high (40-90% reduction), 27 modest (10-40%), 21 little (0-10%), 7 no increase, 9 unknown. citations.claim: The Krefeld flying-insect biomass decline, and the design features that drive the subsequent critique
citations.authors: Caspar A. Hallmann, Martin Sorg, Eelke Jongejans, Henk Siepel, Nick Hofland, Heinz Schwan, Werner Stenmans, Andreas Muller, Hubert Sumser, Thomas Horren, Dave Goulson, Hans de Kroon
citations.venue: PLoS ONE 12(10): e0185809, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0185809
citations.figure: 'Our analysis estimates a seasonal decline of 76%, and mid-summer decline of 82% in flying insect biomass over the 27 years of study.' Malaise traps deployed over 27 years (1989-2016) in 63 nature protection areas in Germany, yielding 96 unique location-year combinations. Critically for uncertainty: 'Most locations (59%, n = 37) were sampled in only one year, 20 locations in two years, five locations in three years, and one in four years' — the trend is inferred largely across space rather than from repeated sampling of the same site, and all sites are Western European low-altitude protected fragments embedded in a human-dominated landscape.

citations.claim: The global meta-analytic revision of the insect-decline rate, which is far smaller than the Krefeld figure and is not uniformly negative

A formal Comment (Science, DOI 10.1126/science.abd8947) disputes the meta-analysis on grounds of errors and biases, and the authors published a Response.

citations.claim: Agricultural soil erosion rates exceed soil formation rates by one to two orders of magnitude
citations.authors: David R. Montgomery

Conventional plow-based agriculture increases erosion rates enough to prove unsustainable, whereas hillslope soil production and erosion evolve to balance in natural systems.

hazards.uncertainty: THE ANNUAL PROBABILITY IS AN AUTHOR ESTIMATE AND IS THE WEAKEST NUMBER IN THIS ENTRY. No published source gives a per-year probability for a composite 'biosphere degradation step', because degradation is a trend rather than a Poisson event; I constructed 3%/yr (roughly one 5-pp step per 20-40 years) by projecting four independently measured rates — HANPP +0.11 pp/yr, fish-stock sustainability -0.57 pp/yr, terrestrial insect abundance -0.92 to -1.11%/yr, High Plains storage -9% over ~70 years. A critic should attack that aggregation directly: the four indicators are not commensurable, and summing them into a single 'attainable calorie supply' fraction is my construction, not anyone's finding. SECOND, the pollinator-to-calorie link is routinely overstated in popular treatments and I have deliberately not used the '35% of food' framing as a calorie figure: Klein's 35% is production VOLUME, dominated by fruits, vegetables and oilseeds, and the staple cereals supplying most calories are wind- or self-pollinated. I could not retrieve this session a published estimate of mortality attributable to pollinator loss (Smith et al. 2015, Lancet, is the relevant paper and I did not fetch it); the 0.0005 deaths_fraction in tier 1 is therefore an author estimate standing in for that unretrieved figure. THIRD, the insect-decline literature is genuinely contested and I have represented both sides: Hallmann's 76%/82% comes from a design in which 59% of locations were sampled in a single year, and van Klink's global meta-analysis puts terrestrial decline at roughly one-tenth the Krefeld rate while finding freshwater insects INCREASING — and van Klink is itself the subject of a formal Comment in Science alleging errors and biases, with a published Response. Any simulator using '75% of insects gone' as a global parameter is using a local, contested figure as a planetary one. FOURTH, the planetary-boundaries framework quantifies transgression, not consequence: Richardson et al. explicitly decline to supply a HANPP-to-yield transfer function, and inventing one is the most likely route by which a model would manufacture doom that the evidence does not support. FIFTH, the High Plains figures are for one basin and the basin mean badly understates the local picture (wells range +86 ft to -265 ft); I did not retrieve a global groundwater-depletion total this session. SIXTH, note the direction-of-error asymmetry: the entire observed record runs the other way — output per capita up 53% since 1961 — so the burden of proof on any lethal coefficient here is high, and I have set no terminal tier because there is no evidential basis for one on a century timescale.

hazards.name: Global food-system shock via multi-breadbasket failure
hazards.oneLine: Simultaneous climate-driven harvest failure in several of the handful of regions that supply most traded grain, converted into famine by export restriction and reserve inaccessibility rather than by the calorie deficit itself.
hazards.mechanism: A multi-breadbasket failure is a single-year, weather-driven collapse of yields in several of the small number of regions that supply most internationally traded grain — US maize, Black Sea and Australian wheat, South Asian rice, Southern Cone soy — driven by the correlated atmospheric patterns (ENSO phases, persistent blocking, jet-stream waveguide states) that can hit them in the same season. The physical deficit is survivable on its face: a 10% global cereal shortfall is about 36 days of world consumption, and carry-over stocks stand at 31.6% of use, roughly 115 days. What kills is the policy response and the distribution of who eats. Exporters insulate their domestic markets: Martin and Anderson attribute 45% of the 2006-08 rise in world rice prices and 30% of the rise in wheat prices to insulating trade behaviour, which is self-cancelling on average across countries while converting a moderate global shortfall into an extreme price shock for the countries that must import. Poor import-dependent households then buy fewer calories and cheaper, less nutritious calories; child wasting and stunting rise; and infectious-disease case-fatality rises in an undernourished population. In states already fragile, the price shock plus the fiscal shock of import subsidies produces unrest and conflict, which disrupts the following season's planting and turns a one-year event into a multi-year one. Almost every death is a famine or epidemic death in a low-income food-deficit importer, months to years after the harvest that failed, and geographically nowhere near the breadbasket that failed.

rate.eventDefinition: A single-year decline of >=10% in global cereal production relative to the preceding three-year mean, arising from simultaneous climate-driven yield failure in three or more major breadbasket regions. Excludes nuclear-winter and volcanic-winter causes, which belong to their own hazard entries and have their own (much larger) severity distributions. This is the probability the SHOCK occurs, not the probability anyone dies from it.
rate.trend: Rising, and this is the best-evidenced trend in the packet. Gaupp et al. find the annual probability of ALL studied breadbaskets simultaneously experiencing climate risk rose from 0.3% to 1.2% for wheat, 0.8% to 1.1% for maize and 1.7% to 2.0% for soybean between 1967-1990 and 1991-2012 — a fourfold rise for wheat within the observational record. Under warming, modelled multiple-breadbasket-failure risk for maize rises from 6% to 40% at 1.5 C and 54% at 2 C. Cottrell et al. independently find 226 food production shocks across 134 nations over 53 years with increasing frequency across all sectors. Countervailing: the buffer trend is favourable, with stock-to-use at 31.6% and 2026/27 the second-largest harvest on record.

rateMods.why: Gaupp et al. measure the probability of synchronous multi-breadbasket wheat failure rising from 0.3% per year (1967-1990) to 1.2% (1991-2012). That is a measured, not assumed, warming coupling — one of the few on the board — reference point solved at build time (2.776) so that the mean multiplier over 100 years is exactly 1: the cited rate was annualised from a by-2100 figure, so its century total must be preserved while the shape is allowed to rise

tiers.label: Price spike, reserves hold
tiers.desc: Reserves are drawn down, world cereal prices roughly double for 12-24 months, and the food-insecure population rises by tens to low hundreds of millions — the 2007-08 and 2010-11 pattern, in which no measurable global excess-mortality signal appeared. Trade stays largely open, the deficit is spread across importers, and the next harvest closes it.
tiers.split: price spike, reserves hold. 5% prompt: this hazard is famine by definition

tiers.label: Export-restriction cascade
tiers.desc: Major exporters ban or tax exports, which is individually rational and collectively catastrophic: the physically available grain exists but does not move. Prices in import-dependent countries rise multiples above the world fundamental (rice rose 117-149% in Q1 2008 on restrictions plus panic buying by importers). Regional famines occur in low-income food-deficit importers and in conflict-affected states; urban unrest and government instability follow the price series with a lag of months.
tiers.split: export-restriction cascade — the 2007-08 and 2010-11 shape

tiers.label: Multi-year deficit, reserves exhausted
tiers.desc: The shock repeats or persists for three or more seasons — the correlated-climate case, or a first-year failure followed by conflict-driven planting failure. Accessible stocks are gone by year two; humanitarian systems are overwhelmed; famine becomes continental rather than national. Livestock herds are slaughtered for grain-sparing, removing the protein base for a decade. Industrial capacity is not destroyed but is diverted, and recovery is limited by rebuilding herds, seed stocks and rural labour.
tiers.split: multi-year deficit, reserves exhausted

tiers.label: Compound collapse
tiers.desc: Harvest failure coincides with a trade shutdown AND an interruption of synthetic nitrogen or phosphate supply for three or more consecutive seasons — the case where the buffer built by hazard 1's degradation has already been spent. Because roughly 48% of the world population is fed on Haber-Bosch nitrogen and the effect hits the entire planted area at once rather than one region, the loss is not regional and not bufferable by stocks. Deaths approach the scale modelled for a regional nuclear winter (>2 billion in Xia et al.'s India-Pakistan case), but seed stock, land, knowledge and most industrial capacity survive, so recovery is a matter of decades rather than never.
tiers.split: compound collapse

cascades.why: food price spikes transmit to unrest and government failure; the 2010-11 literature is contested on causality and the multiplier is kept modest for that reason
undernutrition raises incidence and case-fatality
emergency cropland expansion and fallow-breaking

hazards.uncertainty: WHERE THIS IS WEAKEST, IN ORDER. (1) The headline annual probability of 0.5%/yr is a construction, not a retrieved figure. Gaupp gives 1.1-2.0%/yr for simultaneous CLIMATE RISK across all breadbaskets in a single crop, which is a much weaker condition than a >=10% global cereal shortfall — climate risk in every region does not mean total loss in every region, and a shortfall in one crop is partly offset by others. The observational constraint runs the other way: in 65 years of FAO records there has been NO single-year global cereal production drop approaching 10%, which caps the base rate below about 1.5%/yr. I put the best estimate an order of magnitude below Gaupp's per-crop figure for that reason, and a serious critic could argue for anywhere in 0.1%-2%. (2) The accessible-stocks fraction 'a' is load-bearing and unmeasured here. The 115-day reserve figure is a world aggregate; a large share sits in national strategic reserves that do not enter trade, so an importer's effective buffer is materially smaller. I could not retrieve a figure for that share this session — it is the parameter most likely to change the tier probabilities, and it should be exposed in the simulator rather than baked in. (3) The severity tiers are author judgement calibrated on two real events with very different outcomes: 2007-08 (large price spike, no detectable global excess mortality) and historical policy famines (Bengal 1943, China 1959-61) where distribution failure rather than production failure killed tens of millions. I could not retrieve mortality estimates for either this session, so the tier death fractions are estimates, not citations. The Xia et al. nuclear-winter figures are cited only to bound the extreme tail and should not be read as this hazard's own severity. (4) The Gaupp figures come from search-surfaced abstracts; both papers are paywalled and both returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch. The two Gaupp papers are DIFFERENT studies and it is easy to blend them — the 0.3%-to-1.2% historical probabilities are from the Nature Climate Change paper, the 6%/40%/54% warming projections from the Agricultural Systems paper. Verify that attribution before compiling. (5) NO TERMINAL TIER. A food-system shock, even at the 2-billion-death scale, leaves land, seed stock, agronomic knowledge and most industrial capacity intact; recovery is bounded by herd and seed rebuilding, not by irreversibility. Ord's Table 6.1 puts existential (not catastrophic) risk from non-climate environmental damage at ~1 in 1,000 per century, and I have found no published argument for a mechanism by which agricultural failure alone ends humanity permanently. The XPT gap between catastrophe (9-20%) and extinction (1-6%) across ALL causes reinforces this: a simulator that lets this hazard terminate the run is making a claim no source in this packet supports. (6) Crop diversity is the knob I am least able to quantify: Khoury measures homogeneity of national food SUPPLIES, not the covariance of yield failures, and the step from '50 commodities supply 90% of calories' to a variance multiplier is my inference, not his finding.

hazards.name: VEI-7 / Magnitude-7 explosive eruption (Tambora class)
hazards.oneLine: An eruption of Tambora-1815 scale or larger injects tens of teragrams of sulfur into the stratosphere, cooling the planet by roughly one to two degrees for two to three years and causing simultaneous harvest failures across the mid-latitudes.
hazards.mechanism: A magnitude-7 eruption ejects on the order of 10^14 kg of magma (>=100 km3 bulk tephra) over days to weeks. Proximally, pyroclastic density currents travel 20-100+ km and would erase a city outright; ash fall collapses roofs; rain-remobilised lahars persist for a decade or more. But the global killer is the sulfur. Newhall, Self & Robock note that above roughly 5 Tg SO2 of stratospheric input, eruptions produce noticeable climate impacts; Tambora delivered ~53-60 Tg SO2 and Pinatubo's ~20 Mt SO2 alone lowered global surface temperature by 0.5 degC for two years. The sulfate aerosol veil reflects shortwave radiation, cools land faster than ocean, weakens the Asian and African monsoons and shortens growing seasons in both hemispheres simultaneously. What kills people at scale is then famine and the seizing-up of grain trade, not ash or heat: 1258 (post-Samalas) brought famine, grain-price inflation and the Spitalfields mass graves; 1816 (post-Tambora) brought the Year Without a Summer with famine across Europe, India and China. A modern repeat adds failure modes Tambora did not have: multi-week closure of global airspace, degraded GPS timing, ash-induced power-grid flashovers, and just-in-time food logistics with only months of grain in store.

rate.eventDefinition: An eruption anywhere on Earth delivering stratospheric sulfate forcing at least as large as Tambora 1815 - equivalently VEI >= 7 / magnitude >= 7 for silicic explosive eruptions, but also reachable by high-sulfur basaltic fissure eruptions such as Laki 1783. Best estimate is the ice-core rate of forcing-events exceeding Tambora (Lin et al. 2022: 1.60 per millennium over 60-9 ka). Low bound is Rougier et al. 2018's geological M7 return period of 1200 yr; high bound is Newhall et al. 2018's incompleteness-corrected 2 per millennium.
rate.trend: The eruption rate itself is flat: Lin et al. find the frequency of large eruptions across 60-9 ka is 'rather constant and comparable to that of recent times'. What rises steeply is consequence. World population was ~1 billion at Tambora and is >8 billion now; Newhall et al. record that the area around Campi Flegrei went from ~100,000 people at its last eruption to ~4.4 million, and that 20-30 million people now live within 100 km of several Indonesian and Philippine VEI-7 candidates. Supply-chain interdependence and thin grain reserves raise vulnerability further; forecasting, aid capacity and stored calories partly offset it.

tiers.label: Remote vent, single eruption
tiers.desc: The eruption occurs at one of the many candidate volcanoes in the Kuriles, Aleutians, Kamchatka or the Andes with <1 million people inside 100 km, or is sulfur-poor. Proximal deaths in the thousands to low hundreds of thousands. Global cooling of ~0.5-1 K for 1-2 years produces one or two poor harvests; famine concentrated in import-dependent low-income countries; grain price spikes and export bans. Aviation disrupted for weeks over one or more continents.
tiers.split: remote vent: the deaths are proximal and prompt

tiers.label: Tambora repeat near a population centre, or high sulfur yield
tiers.desc: Either the vent is one of the Indonesian, Philippine, Italian, Japanese or Central American candidates with millions inside 100 km - Newhall et al. state a VEI-7 near an urban area today could kill millions and that no evacuation of millions for months has ever been achieved - or the sulfur yield puts global land cooling near or above Tambora's -1.9 degC. Two to three consecutive globally poor harvests; multi-year famine across South Asia, the Sahel and the Horn; refugee flows needing food and shelter for months to years; sustained trade and financial disruption.
tiers.split: a Tambora repeat. 1815 gave the Year Without a Summer and a European subsistence crisis — the deaths were overwhelmingly famine and typhus, not pyroclastic flow

tiers.label: Clustered eruptions or a hit on an already-stressed food system
tiers.desc: The worst realistic VEI-7 outcome: either a cluster of large sulfur-rich eruptions within years to decades (as in CE 1257, 1268, 1275, 1284, whose additive forcing Newhall et al. link to the onset of the Little Ice Age and a sustained ~0.5 K depression), or a single event landing on a food system already stressed by war, drought or export blockade. Cooling persists 5-10 years with decadal-to-centennial ocean-sea-ice feedback. Widespread famine, grain-export nationalism, state failure and resource conflict; Newhall et al. explicitly note that desperate populations now have modern weapons and that analogies have been drawn to nuclear-war scenarios.
tiers.split: clustered eruptions, or a hit on an already-stressed food system. Newhall et al.: multiple sulfur-rich eruptions within years of each other compound

hazards.uncertainty:
Frequency: the three estimates span a factor of 2.4 (0.83 to 2.0 per millennium) and are not independent - Newhall's 'closer to 2 per millennium' is an incompleteness-corrected reading of the same Holocene record that Rougier's 1200-yr figure is derived from. The single most attackable step in this entry is the event definition: Lin et al.'s 1.60/millennium counts SULFUR-FORCING events exceeding Tambora, not VEI-7 eruptions, and these sets differ in both directions. Laki 1783 is the archetypal false negative - a VEI 4 fissure eruption that released ~120 Mt SO2 - while a sulfur-poor VEI 7 would be a false positive. I have deliberately defined the hazard by forcing rather than by VEI because forcing is what drives the famine, but a critic could reasonably object that the resulting rate is then not 'the VEI-7 rate' and should not be labelled as such.

Severity: much weaker than frequency. Tambora's -1.9 +/- 0.2 degC is a global LAND anomaly for 1816 (Wilson et al. 2023); the commonly quoted 0.4-0.7 degC is the global land-plus-ocean mean, and quoting the land number as a global mean is a common and serious error - the simulator must not conflate them. Tambora's global death toll is poorly constrained: direct deaths are of order 10^5, but 1816-1817 famine mortality and the subsequent cholera pandemic are contested and much larger, and Newhall et al. quote Guillet et al. and Campbell cautioning that some post-Samalas famines started before the eruption and cannot all be attributed to it. All deaths_fraction values in the severity tiers are AUTHOR ESTIMATES: no published figure exists for the fraction of a 2026 world population killed by a VEI-7, and the tier probabilities are my own partition of a space with one modern data point in it.

The evacuation_lead_days parameter is the weakest quantified knob. Newhall et al. give the qualitative facts (hours-to-days final runup; never millions evacuated for months) but no survival-versus-lead-time curve exists; the saturating form I give is an author construction.

What I could NOT verify this session: the full text of Cassidy & Mani 2022 (Nature 608:469-471) is paywalled, so the widely circulated '1 in 6 chance of a magnitude-7 eruption this century' is sourced here to Wilson et al. 2023, who state it in that exact form, rather than to Cassidy & Mani. The Cabaniss et al. 2018 GRL figures are quoted from a ScienceDaily summary, not the paper. Both are flagged in the citations above.

hazards.name: VEI-8 / Magnitude-8 supereruption (Toba class)
hazards.oneLine: A magnitude-8 eruption injects hundreds of teragrams of sulfur into the stratosphere, producing a volcanic winter of several kelvin lasting years to a decade and a simultaneous, global failure of agriculture.
hazards.mechanism: A magnitude-8 eruption discharges of order 10^15 kg (about 1000 Gt) of magma - Toba's Youngest Toba Tuff is estimated at more than 2800-5300 km3 dense rock equivalent, forming a 3500 km2 caldera. Proximal effects are total but geographically bounded: pyroclastic flows sterilise an area hundreds of kilometres across, and centimetre-to-metre ash blankets cover subcontinental areas. The global mechanism is again sulfate. Ice-core sulfur-isotope work puts the stratospheric loading of the Toba candidate horizons at 72-233 Tg S, two to four times the 1257 Samalas eruption and roughly 7-23 times Pinatubo. That veil cools the surface by several kelvin, cuts precipitation, collapses the monsoons and shortens or eliminates growing seasons across the mid-latitudes for years. Nobody dies of the eruption itself outside the proximal zone; they die of famine, of the collapse of grain trade and of the conflict that follows, over the two to ten years the veil persists. Ozone destruction of up to 60% after large caldera-forming eruptions, recovering over one to two decades, adds a UV stress on top of the cold. Crucially, the one M8 in the human record did NOT produce a demographic collapse: archaeological sites in India, Sumatra and South Africa show occupation continuing across the 74 ka ash, and no genomic bottleneck coincides with that date.

rate.eventDefinition: A magnitude-8 explosive eruption anywhere on Earth, defined by Rougier et al. as at least 1000 Gt (10^15 kg) of erupted mass. Best estimate is the reciprocal of their 17 ka return period; low and high are the reciprocals of the upper and lower ends of their 95% credible interval (48 ka and 5.2 ka). Note that the folk figure of 1 in 50,000 yr (2e-5 /yr) sits at the extreme LOW end of this interval, and that an independent ice-core estimate - Lin et al.'s 0.07 eruptions per millennium with climate forcing at or above Taupo Oruanui, i.e. 7e-5 /yr - lands almost exactly on the best estimate.
rate.trend: Flat over the coming century. No anthropogenic mechanism alters magma supply on that timescale, and Lin et al. find the large-eruption frequency constant across 60-9 ka. One weak upward mechanism is worth recording but not applying: Lin et al. observe a marked rise in large Northern Hemisphere eruptions during the deglacial period 16-9 ka and attribute it to isostatic unloading of the NH ice sheets, so sustained large-scale ice loss is a plausible long-run forcing of volcanism - but the implied lag is millennial and the effect on this century's M8 rate is negligible. What does change is exposure: a globally integrated, low-inventory, mid-latitude-dependent food system is more vulnerable to a multi-year cold shock than the subsistence agriculture of any previous century, even as total stored calories and technical adaptive capacity are far greater.

tiers.label: Attenuated - aerosol microphysics limits the forcing
tiers.desc: The eruption is extratropical, sulfur-poor, or - most importantly - the injection is so large that aerosol microphysics blunts it: bigger droplets scatter less per unit mass and sediment faster, so forcing scales far below linearly with sulfur mass. This is the Timmreck et al. reading of Toba, and it is what the archaeological record of 74 ka actually supports. Global cooling of 1-2 K for 2-5 years; proximal deaths in the millions to tens of millions; multi-year famine in import-dependent regions; severe but survivable damage to global agriculture and trade.
tiers.split: attenuated — aerosol microphysics limits the forcing. This tier exists because the forcing exponent is the single largest disagreement in supereruption science

tiers.label: Volcanic winter
tiers.desc: Tropical vent, high sulfur yield. Global cooling of 3-5 K sustained for 5-10 years with decadal ocean and sea-ice feedbacks; monsoon failure across Asia and Africa; three or more consecutive near-total harvest failures in the mid-latitude breadbaskets. Grain export bans become universal; the ~10^9 people who depend on imported staples are the first to die, followed by urban populations everywhere as distribution fails. Industrial capacity survives in fragments; global institutions do not.
tiers.split: volcanic winter

tiers.label: Decade without a summer
tiers.desc: Upper end of the plausible forcing range: 5-8 K global cooling persisting a decade or more, at or beyond the top of what any modern civilisation has faced. Conventional outdoor agriculture fails across all mid- and high-latitude land for several consecutive years. Deaths are overwhelmingly from famine and the wars fought over the remaining food; survival concentrates in low-latitude coastal and island regions with fisheries access, and wherever resilient-food production (seaweed, methane single-cell protein, cellulosic sugar, greenhouses) has been pre-positioned. Industrial civilisation is set back generations but the species persists.
tiers.split: a decade without a summer. Note the ratio: 1% of the deaths are from the eruption and 99% from the harvests it prevents

tiers.label: Terminal
tiers.desc: Humanity does not recover. This requires the cold shock to be compounded - by nuclear exchange over remaining food-producing land, by the permanent loss of the accessible fossil and mineral base needed to re-industrialise, or by a residual population too small and too scattered to sustain a technological society. Note that this tier is NOT supported by the 74 ka record, where a genuine M8 failed to bottleneck a hunter-gatherer humanity of far fewer people with far less technology; it is included because modern civilisation has failure modes that hunter-gatherers did not.
tiers.split: the tail. The Toba genetic-bottleneck claim that used to justify this tier is now contested — several genetic analyses find no bottleneck coinciding with Toba

cascades.why: the canonical natural abrupt-sunlight-reduction scenario
grain export bans and mass migration under a decade-long cooling
ashfall and a collapsing demand base

hazards.uncertainty:
WARNING ASYMMETRY (applies to both volcanic entries and should be modelled explicitly). The warning we would get and the warning we could act on are different things. Long-lead: silicic caldera systems are expected to inflate for a very long time before a catastrophic eruption - Cabaniss, Gregg & Grosfils 2018 expect 'tens to hundreds of meters of uplift' over 'hundreds to thousands of years' of rejuvenation, far larger than any unrest observed today. Short-lead: that long signal does not resolve into a date. Newhall et al. 2018 report that at Rabaul, Campi Flegrei and Pinatubo, 'despite prolonged early unrest, the final runup to eruption was just hours to days', that 'an eruption was imminent did not become clear until hours to days before those eruptions', and that 'most unrest at calderas dies out rather than culminates in eruption' - so the base rate of false alarms is high and the cost of acting on them is enormous. And there is no prevention: no proposed intervention on a magma chamber of this size has any empirical support. The honest model is therefore decades of ambiguous warning, days of unambiguous warning, and zero mitigation of the event itself - which makes pre-positioned resilience (food, not evacuation) the only lever with real expected value.

FREQUENCY. The Rougier 17 ka figure rests on very few M8 events in LaMEVE and its 95% CI spans nearly an order of magnitude (5.2-48 ka). A serious critic would say the under-recording correction is doing all the work: moving the return period from ~50 ka to 17 ka is a modelling choice about how fast the geological record degrades with age, not a new observation. The independent ice-core corroboration (Lin et al., 0.07 per millennium) is reassuring but is itself based on n = 3 events in a 51 kyr window, and it measures sulfur forcing rather than erupted mass - the two are only loosely coupled. Two weak estimates agreeing is weaker evidence than it looks.

SEVERITY - THE WEAKEST PART OF THIS ENTRY BY FAR. There is exactly one M8 in the human record and the modelled climate impact spans a factor of about eight: 7-19 K under naive linear scaling from Pinatubo (Jones et al. 2005; Robock et al. 2009) versus 'far less than the size of the eruption might suggest' once aerosol microphysics is included (Timmreck et al. 2010). Both are reported in Newhall et al. 2018 without adjudication. That is why I have exposed the scaling exponent as an explicit parameter rather than burying a choice inside a fixed cooling figure - a simulator that hard-codes the linear form will overstate this hazard by an order of magnitude in deaths.

The empirical arbiter cuts toward the low end: Toba did not bottleneck humanity. Occupation continues across the 74 ka ash in India, Sumatra and South Africa, and no genomic bottleneck coincides with that date - the bottleneck signal in the human genome is at ~50 ka and is an out-of-Africa founder effect. Anyone using the 'Toba nearly killed us all' framing is using a claim that the field has largely abandoned. The honest counter-argument is that this is not reassuring in the way it first appears: 74 ka hunter-gatherers were mobile, low-density, locally self-provisioning and tropical, whereas a modern population of eight billion depends on a small number of mid-latitude breadbaskets, a few months of stored grain, and a globally integrated distribution system - exactly the configuration a multi-year mid-latitude cold shock breaks. The past under-states the modern risk on the vulnerability axis while over-stating it on the forcing axis.

ALL deaths_fraction AND p_given_event VALUES IN THE SEVERITY TIERS ARE AUTHOR ESTIMATES. No published study gives the fraction of a 2026 world population killed by an M8. The terminal tier's p_given_event of 0.015 is anchored on Ord's reported ~1 in 10,000 per century existential estimate divided by this entry's ~0.6% per century M8 rate; I obtained Ord's figures from a secondary source (an EA Forum post by Cassidy & Mani) because I could not retrieve the text of The Precipice this session, and the figure should be treated as an expert's subjective prior, not a derived result. The recovery_years value of 100000 in the terminal tier is a sentinel meaning 'never', not an estimate.

I could not retrieve any Existential Risk Persuasion Tournament figure specific to supervolcanoes, and no such number is reported here. I also could not retrieve the full text of Cassidy & Mani 2022 (Nature 608:469-471) or Rougier et al. 2018 itself - the Rougier abstract quoted above is verbatim from the University of Bristol's institutional record, and the M7 return period of 1200 yr is quoted from Lohmann & Svensson 2022 citing Rougier, not from Rougier directly.

hazards.name: Dependence of the food supply on Haber-Bosch synthetic nitrogen
hazards.oneLine: About half of humanity is fed on nitrogen fixed industrially from natural gas, applied fresh every season by a few hundred plants with no stockpile behind them.
hazards.mechanism: Crops remove nitrogen from soil every harvest, and industrial ammonia synthesis is what puts it back at current yields. Around 100 Tg of Haber-Bosch nitrogen goes into global agriculture each year at an energy cost of at least 32 MJ per kg of nitrogen fixed, roughly one percent of global primary energy, and roughly 80 percent of all manufactured nitrogen goes into fertilizer. There is no meaningful buffer: fertilizer is applied within months of being made, and soil organic nitrogen cannot carry current yields for more than a season or two. If ammonia output stops, yields of the four staples fall by 35-48 percent within one to two growing seasons, and the deaths are famine deaths concentrated in dense, import-dependent, high-yield-dependent regions — not deaths from the interruption itself. The dependency is doubly fragile because it runs on pipeline natural gas, which is itself dependent on the electricity grid.

rate.eventDefinition: a sustained reduction of at least 50 percent in global Haber-Bosch ammonia output for at least twelve consecutive months
rate.trend: Roughly flat to slightly rising in the near term. The 2021-22 European gas price shock curtailed a large share of EU ammonia capacity without moving global output much, which shows the tail is real but also that capacity is geographically diversified (notably coal-based Chinese production). The dominant consideration is that this event is almost always a CONSEQUENCE of another hazard — infrastructure loss, great-power war, an extreme energy shock — rather than a standalone failure, so its rate is largely inherited.

rateMods.why: Haber-Bosch is an industrial process consuming at least 32 MJ per kg of nitrogen fixed. A damaged industrial base is precisely what stops it, which makes this hazard the main channel by which infrastructure loss becomes starvation

tiers.label: Regional fertilizer famine
tiers.desc: One major producing or importing region loses fertilizer supply for one to two seasons. Yields there fall by a third or more; the region becomes a large net importer at exactly the moment world stocks are being drawn down.
tiers.split: regional fertiliser famine — 2% prompt, this is a food hazard end to end

tiers.label: Global staple yield collapse
tiers.desc: Global loss of industrial fertilizer, alongside the pesticide, irrigation and mechanization inputs that usually fail with it. Modelled yield reductions with no industrial inputs are -35% rice, -37% wheat, -41% soybeans, -48% corn. Global calorie supply falls by roughly 40 percent while the population that those calories currently feed remains the same.
tiers.split: global staple yield collapse. Erisman et al. put the share of humanity fed by synthetic nitrogen at ~48%

tiers.label: Fertilizer loss compounding a sunlight reduction or full infrastructure loss
tiers.desc: Industrial nitrogen and sunlight both fail. The 40 percent input-driven yield loss stacks multiplicatively on the up-to-90 percent sunlight-driven loss in the worst year of a severe nuclear winter. Nothing recognizable as industrial agriculture survives the first three years.
tiers.split: compounding a sunlight reduction or a full infrastructure loss

cascades.why: fertiliser interruption shows up as a yield shortfall one to two seasons later

citations.claim: Staple crop yield reductions in the absence of industrial agricultural inputs
citations.authors: Juan B. García Martínez, Jeffray Behr, Joshua M. Pearce, David C. Denkenberger, reporting Moersdorf, Rivers, Denkenberger, Breuer & Jehn (2024, Global Challenges, Wiley)
citations.venue: ALLFED preprint, EarthArXiv (version 08/2024)

hazards.uncertainty: The annual probability is explicitly an AUTHOR ESTIMATE. I found no published frequency estimate for a sustained global ammonia-output collapse, and I have not dressed one up: the figure is a judgment anchored on the observation that the 2021-22 European gas crisis curtailed a large regional share without approaching a 50 percent global cut. The weakest link in the whole hazard is the step from '48 percent of humanity is fed by Haber-Bosch nitrogen' to any deaths_fraction. Erisman's 48 percent is a counterfactual nitrogen-balance accounting figure — it says how much of current food production is attributable to synthetic N under stated assumptions (including that other improvements would have accounted for a 20 percent productivity increase between 1950 and 2000), not that 48 percent of people die if it stops. Smil's independent estimate of 40 percent for 2000 differs from Erisman's 44 percent for the same year, which is a fair indication of the method's precision. A serious critic would attack three things: (1) that the substitution_shortfall factor of 0.3-0.7 in the first parameter is entirely mine and unsupported by any published study I retrieved; (2) that the Moersdorf yield figures are modelled, not observed, and come from an ALLFED-affiliated group whose institutional interest is in the fragility being real; (3) that I read those figures out of a non-peer-reviewed ALLFED preprint quoting the peer-reviewed paper rather than out of the peer-reviewed paper itself, because the Wiley page returned HTTP 403 this session.

hazards.name: Interdependent infrastructure cascade and the black-start trap
hazards.oneLine: The electricity grid, the gas network and the communications network each require the other two to function, so a large enough failure in any one of them does not stop there.
hazards.mechanism: Critical infrastructures are coupled physically (gas turbines need pipeline pressure; pipeline compressors need grid power), cyber-physically (grid control needs SCADA telemetry; SCADA needs powered communications), geographically (co-located rights of way), and logically. Buldyrev et al. show that this coupling changes the qualitative behaviour of the system rather than merely degrading it: interdependent networks fragment through a discontinuous, first-order transition at a much higher connectivity than a single network needs, and a broader degree distribution — hub-heavy, like every real infrastructure — makes them MORE fragile to random failure rather than less. The concrete trap is black start: 60 percent of the black-start resources registered with NERC are gas turbines, wind and solar contribute zero, nuclear plants cannot black-start at all under NRC rules, and a cold coal unit cannot be synchronized for more than 48 hours. Deaths do not come from the loss of light; they come from the loss of water pumping, refrigeration of medicines and food, hospital function, fuel distribution, and — beyond a few weeks — the fertilizer and food chain.

rate.eventDefinition: a North American blackout of at least 186,000 MW of load — the size Hines, Apt and Talukdar compute as the 100-year event from NERC data for 1984-2006
rate.trend: Not improving. Hines et al. find the frequency of large blackouts in the United States has not decreased over time even after controlling for demand and population growth, and they find strong statistical support for a power-law relationship between blackout size and frequency, meaning the tail does not thin. Two trends push in opposite directions: rising inverter-based generation removes rotational inertia and contributes zero registered black-start capability, while grid-scale batteries have now been demonstrated as black-start sources (a 33 MW / 20 MWh lithium-ion system starting a 44 MW combined-cycle plant).

rateMods.why: hardening reduces the rate of the large events; reference 0.15 is the present, poorly-quantified level of transformer protection and held spares

tiers.label: Days-scale blackout restored by black start
tiers.desc: A cascading outage takes down a large fraction of an interconnection; black-start units and cranking paths work as planned and bulk service returns within one to three days. Deaths from heat, cold, medical device failure and traffic; economic loss dominates.
tiers.split: days-scale blackout restored by black start

tiers.label: Weeks-scale outage with gas and water failure
tiers.desc: Black start is delayed because gas compressor stations lost power, gas-fired black-start units cannot get fuel, and coal units are past their 48-hour cold-start window. Municipal water pumping and sewage treatment fail after their few days of on-site reserve. Disease and dehydration mortality begins; the fuel distribution network stops because pumps are electric.
tiers.split: weeks-scale outage with gas and water failure — half the deaths prompt (heat, cold, medical), half through food

tiers.label: Months-scale continental grid loss
tiers.desc: Extra-high-voltage transformers are physically damaged — geomagnetic storm, HEMP, coordinated physical or cyber attack — and replacement lead times run to months or years. Industrial agriculture, ammonia synthesis, refrigeration, water and medical infrastructure all stop across a continent for a growing season or more.
tiers.split: months-scale continental grid loss

cascades.why: no grid, no ammonia
cold chains, irrigation pumping and rail

citations.authors: Sergey V. Buldyrev, Roni Parshani, Gerald Paul, H. Eugene Stanley, Shlomo Havlin

And: "While for a single network a broader degree distribution of the network nodes results in higher robustness to random failure, for interdependent networks, the broader the distribution is, the more vulnerable the networks become to random failure."
